title: R.L. Stine's Pumpkinhead 2
my_review: It’s fine, albeit it feels a bit stiff. Like it’s dancing around some aspects awkwardly for budgetary reasons

title: Godzilla Minus Zero
my_review: An extremely worthy sequel to its predecessor, really amping up most every aspect from the first. It doesn’t have quite the same potency in the human side, despite that aspect getting amped up the most, but the spectacle of kaju nonsense is just so damn glorious here. Also, goddamn, what a hype theme.

title: Crawlers
my_review: Not crazy about movies that just top to bottom look visually unappealing in the setting and context. So it wasn’t helping that it’s also just very mediocre. Had some interesting ideas, but it didn’t lean hard enough on them. Like the latex catsuit battle gear was a wild choice but not against it, but maybe make it proactively effective(though, stop having people take off their protective headgear to…emote?) I’d want more of that, just weaponizing what they have in the building, instead of everyone just getting swarmed and dying in dumb scenes. Matilda Lutz is much better than what she stars in.

title: Beware Boiúna
my_review: A bold move to kill Jessica Rothe aswell as the rest of the cast so early into shit hitting the fan, but like whatta downgrade and what feels like a waste of time spent developing characters. Really the movie seems obsessed with this subversive decision making and that is indeed bold and sometimes that does payoff, but it strips out the narrative payoff. Cause by the end I just wasn’t jazzed about anything we were left with, it feeling like it had a destination in mind and it not putting in the work to get there as much as build up the casualties to sprinkle along the way. I do think the story suffering might be inpart due to budgetary constraint—a giant snake ain’t cheap and neither are needless actors. But it’s not like there’s a way to have it both ways and still be good. That said, I did feel the way it handled the snake was pretty well done. Like this is probably better directed than any ‘Anaconda’ movie, but yeah, I can’t say the story’s much better—as goofy as ‘Anaconda’ movies are.

title: The Cycle
my_review:
It’s a neat idea and some of its execution is inspired, but honestly I think the direction was lacking here. It’s kinda dragging its feet around for a bit, yet even when it picks up or moments happen—it’s not very good? It just wasn’t hitting when it felt like it should. Like when it kicks off it is again—a pretty neat idea, but it looks kinda hokey cause they’re being to ‘loud’ about it. Often feeling like it was showing way too much, or rather the way it was showing itself was just not that great—like the final few minutes in particular looked a lack lustre to me.

Also the casting was maybe partially to blame? I love Deborah Anne Woll & don’t mind the ‘Burn Notice’-guy at all(I’ve never seen ‘Burn Notice’), but some of these other characters just didn’t feel like they fit in? Like Woll’s character’s dad just doesn’t look in the slightest like her father or even very fatherly and that made me never buy into that dynamic which is supposed to be pivotal to the greater theme of the movie. I know this is the case for plenty of movies, but it really was felt here that Woll & ‘Burn Notice’ were like the biggest names they could get and the rest were either already banked on as friends or just what were in the budget. Not to come off as rude as that sounds, as I think they all did fine, but I did feel like Woll & ‘Burn Notice’ were clear standouts here.


I feel I’m being mean and nitpicking towards this. It was fine, just maybe felt too so-so for me, but the ambition was there which is admirable.

title: Onslaught
my_review: Didn’t resonate too much with this one. I’ve been a fan of Adam Wingard(& Dan Stevens) since ‘The Guest’(2014) and have always kept a watchful eye on what he’s up to, hoping for another that works as well as that one did for me. So this seemed promising, Dan Stevens inclusion aside, its general premise seemed similar and fun enough and while it feels very much like a more updated—and expensive ‘The Guest’, there’s not much of a movie beyond the action, of which is pretty so-so, for me. As others are sure to point out, it largely feels like aura farming for a majority of the film and then some conflict and then a lil’ bit of some really campy story. I’m sure it’s by design, but in the end I just wasn’t really that invested with anything. Like for example: even our super soldier “slashers” I wasn’t invested with. The three look the same, all get wordy backstories and introductions but they’re kinda meaningless since that personality is void from any of them. They act like Jason Vorhees/Michael Meyers-types, just silent and violent, but I can’t say their outfits are near iconic enough to work to the same effect as either classic slasher. They mostly just look like cringey military larpers decked out in army surplus & mall ninja gear for a ‘hot’ Facebook photoshoot. One gets given a link to our heroine and it… means nothing, she beat him then and beats him again with very little time given to any shared history or vendetta, almost feel like he should’ve sought her out rather than gotten lucky. They’re also just not that impressive, they mostly just escape a facility and shootup a gas station, but then just get stalled up at a trailer park by three plucky civilians with limited means to defend against. Nothing they did ever felt as cool as them just standing there menacingly because when they do act it’s just uneventful. Probably due to budget, but if you have three super soldier slashers, you’d better be throwing waves of people at them. Like how lame is it that this ‘cleaner’-specialist never encounters them with his team. And then for the actual story, meh. I didn’t care much for the weird kinky doctor who dies very early, that whole part seeming there to give Dan Stevens more time to be a hammy German scientist again aswell as reunite with Rebecca Ferguson. Felt like a waste of both, in low screentime and just not doing much. Adria Arjona also didn’t do much for me either. She’s awesome, but this part is just very unmemorable. It doesn’t feel like she gets near enough a chance to show her badassery as like the main girl in ‘You’re Next’(2011). When she does stuff it’s over and done with, which is boring for both an action movie and a horror movie when there’s so few instances of carnage.  I think alot of my issues were aspects that were very intentional, but it felt like that intentionality led to “shortcuts” undermining the movie as a whole.  Shortcuts in just skimming past things because it’s “that sorta movie”. And for me, I think it could still be that nostalgic movie Wingard wanted to make, but also a good—better, as I didn’t hate this—movie.

my_review: Lived up to the hype

title: Soulm8te
my_review: So actually this kinda worked for me? It’s not great to be honest, but it also feels aware of that fact and that’s really all I want from this sorta premise. Megan Fox’s horrendous ‘Subservience’(2024) movie thinks this is the movie it was setting out to make, but it was non-committal and merely seemed to fall back on Megan Fox’s ‘PG-13 hot factor’ as all it needed and ultimately just felt like a watered down movie that failed at being schlocky horror and/or an erotic-thriller. This movie goes for it though and I think that pays off. It goes for the schlocky horror, it goes for the erotic-thriller and it feels very earnest in how far it’s willing to go to deliver on that. In a lot of ways it’s probably the best murder-android of late next to maybe ‘Companion’(2025), though even then—and this is probably a hottake as I believe that movie was generally well liked—this movie just felt a bit more entertaining to me.  It’s fun, is just fucky enough and it’s silly yet competent enough to not feel patronizing. Could have gone harder and sillier, but for what it is as a mainstream horror, it’s pretty serviceable and apparently amongst others that feels a rarity with what this movie fashions itself as. I had a good time, cause It’s some good schlock. I’d readily take more of these over ‘M3GAN’(2022) if they stuck to the same template(not whatever the fuck ‘M3GAN 2.0’(2025) was going for, keep this stupid sexy fun)

title: The Devil's Mouth
my_review: It’s okay as a survival/natural horror, though I couldn’t muster any care about any of them surviving except this(‘cept for the tour guide who did nothing wrong).

title: Kill Trip
my_review: Very evident what this movie is from the get-go and that’s not inherently a bad thing, a cheap schlocky horror has been known to hit. Looks decent, campy acting & dialogue and a premise that lends itself to a slasher. Problem is that I don’t think they really had enough of a script to fill the runtime. Several scenes feel like characters just repeating their same talking points, even responding with the same responses. Like some poorly edited porno that included multiple takes, where they do and say the same thing but from a different angles and somehow decide to include both variants. They probably had an outline and plot points, but literally nothing else. Also despite the premise, this really doesn’t amount to much of anything. Kills are weak and sparse, plus—this doesn’t even really lend itself to being much of a “horny” slasher—which I do feel it’s kinda aiming for. Without the gratuitous kills or needless objectification of bodies, there’s just no fun to be had since its budget is so low that it can’t get together anything active to compensate, like a party, or the whole festival they’re trying to get to, just something to fill the space where in typical slashers there’d be people suckin’, fuckin’ & duckin’. There is some tethering narrative that feels like it’s from left field with how underdeveloped it is. Especially when it ends and you don’t feel like the journey matches at all with what you saw, it delivering on things it never properly gave time to gestate, or some it did have the time and it’s still just a whiff cause they just didn’t do it right. Dissapointing. I can give a lot of leeway if it’s atleast some fun camp, or ‘cheap but inspired’(a lá ‘Texas Chainsaw Massacre’(1974) and I was totally prepared to for this, but it just really seemed a waste of time overall.

title: Water Park Shark
my_review:
Not quite as silly as you’d think. Oddly ends up feeling like those hokey low budget family movies for much of the movie. So much so you kinda forget it’s wanting you to think it’s some dumb schlocky shark movie—especially with the scarcity of actual shark attacks. Sometimes that helps make the shark attacks funnier—to spoil one that did get me, a shark swallows a random person whole while they were playing around in the park and it’s never addressed. But at the same time, it’s also just kinda weird when carnage & gore does take place, cause it just feels so out of place here to see bodies ripped apart or sharks blown into chum whilst the most juvenile and corny story takes place with the corniest characters. 

So don’t expect ‘Sharknado’(2013)-levels of insanity, or ‘Piranha 3D’(2010)-levels of schlocky nudity & gore, cause I think that’s exactly what this movie wants you to expect and just not really deliver much of either—which is dissapointing, I’d say.

title: Black Box
my_review: Expected far worse, but can’t say it drastically subverted that expectation. It’s kinda a decent watch though. The mystery’s fun as we slowly realize how fucked these people are. Where it does falter is just the writing of the characters that’s really janky. Often times I don’t think people were doing rational things and it leads to a lot of that jankiness. Like when they “land” and only see white lights, nobody tries to open the door. There’s reason why they think they’re being held in the plane, but nobody once checked to see if they could even open the door and try to wave the “black site people” down to explain. This would be impossible we later learn as it’s aliens and they’re in the sky still, but these people don’t know that and there’s no reason not to try.  Or there was a really kinda strange and funny scene with the air marshal. She’s acting hella shady the whole time she maintains order and we later realize it’s for no reason, she’s just aggressive and mysterious by nature. But the moment that got me is when she goes to the stewardesses and says “Pilots’re not responding” Stewardess understandably exclaims “Oh no, really?!” pretty mildly, as if it was just an inconvenience to their predicament Marshal then goes like “CALM DOWN! DON’T PANIC NOW…” just super aggro. I dunno, it stuck out to me cause it was so awkward an interaction, I don’t even believe there was a cut, to say that they tried two different takes, one with a hysterical stewardess and one where they’re calmly discussing matters, it’s both and it’s so goofy. Also a mild issue as it was already mostly done, but they killed off all the “main side characters” pretty quick at the big unveilment of aliens and so at the every end we have to random ass jabronies alongside the main people and it’s so weird cause they’re talking a lot and they have not talked at all the whole movie. The three young adults are our tertiary protagonists and only one makes it past the first hurdle and then he’s taken out pretty quick and we’re left with to rando people we’ve never met before—it’s just really weird and not good writing, in my opinion. Least we can have is a slight introduction to any of those people.  Also why did they just leave the dude to be “crazy” and be the hero, he literally didn’t earn it and “lost” and they just gave up at the finish line. Instead opting to just gaslight him instead. They even just point blank tell him the whole invasion plan to make him… crazier? They didn’t even really need a patsy, they seemed totally content with just being “what happened” after all the craziness. Seems way better to just convert him and have no loose ends. And that’s just another issue I had in that the aliens are just all over the place, they’re huge and lethal and tentaclly, but also body snatchers and tiny insects and they have force fields, they just seemed to operate on “whatever was needed to seem interesting” rather than actually designed and thought out. But that they also just don’t have any reason like a time limit or inability to convert the main dude, they just don’t so he can just have a tragic end, which I don’t think they’d care about in the slightest. Also didn’t they just revive his dead girlfriend(that did feel like a betrayal to the hint of a ship between him and the stewardess, him just randomly getting a freshly dead wife), they showed they could just “revive” people willy nilly, heck it seemed like she kinda was his wife, just taken over rather than entirely being driven by an alien(could be a ‘The Thing’(1982) situation aswell) As an aside, I thought the initial opening seemed way too interesting a way to unravel a story and though I don’t quite mind them not doing that for this, I can’t deny that I couldn’t stop thinking of a much better movie/show in my head of this sort of story. Like the games ‘Her Story’ or ‘Return Of The Obra Dinn’, where you’re seeing fragments of a story being pieced together. ‘Her Story’ having you be a cop sifting through interviews sorted by tags that you can search and watch in an asynchronous order, piecing together a narrative of what happened. ‘Return If The Obra Dinn’ being a less abstract version of that, as you play a 19th century insurance claims officer uncovering what became of a merchant ship’s entire crew that perished with a handy pocket watch that magically takes you to the points in time you find through leftover clues of disturbance, cuing you into a grander event of what happened and caused that evidence to be left as you try to identify each ship inhabitant and how they perished. Both very different games, but they really thrive on that storytelling and I find them both immensely compelling for anyone that likes to find rabbit holes. That’s kinda what the beginning was lending itself towards for me, seeing the remnants of a catastrophe through people’s phones archiving the events. I started thinking how cool that’d be to tell a story like this, investigators making an order out of several random people’s “diaries” and other archival material, slowly deciphering exactly what happened. Barely a whiff of that in this movie and unfair to hold it to my own runaway thoughts, but—what could’ve been. But yeah, okay movie, especially when I expected actual trash movie. Does go a little off the rails in a narrative sense though, like could’ve used a few more drafts to become something kinda decent.

title: Hungry
my_review: Not much of a movie here until like two-thirds in about when Joaquim de Almeida becomes more involved and things start happening. But even when it does get going, there’s just nothing all that interesting going on. Lame characters, well-tread beats, sparsely used hippo, cloud of blood deaths… It’s just not that fun, nor that thrilling, nor that dramatic, so it’s just very bland, in turn.

title: Passenger
my_review:
I think a roadtrip horror movie actually still feels fairly unexplored as a setting and having them be fresh nomads even moreso. Even didn’t hate the general story of this couple on the road. Where the movie just loses me completely is that the actual monster’s just agonizingly unremarkable and the general horror just so vanilla. 

For a real roadtrip horror that utilizes its road setting to the fullest—‘Nocturnal Animals’(2016)

title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
my_review: I liked it, though I’m not entirely smitten with it like I’m sure some people will be. ‘ll probably suffer from a case of “false advertisement” with a good few. Like for me, I did go in kinda expect something more conventionally slasher/horror-based from not knowing much beyond the poster. Though the realization of this being the same director behind ‘I Saw The TV Glow’(2024) helped temper things pretty quickly. I feel you gotta go into these with the right headspace, like not really see them as the conventional movies they liken themselves towards. Like ‘I Saw The TV Glow’ & especially this movie, they have this sorta impassioned “love letter” aspect to them, both pertaining a slew of emotions wrought from what was watched. ‘I Saw The TV Glow’ being one that felt more for the viewer, a more abstract feeling that likened itself to something abstract within the realm of horror due to the emotions that stir up. While with this, it felt more centered on a particular genre/series—‘Sleepaway Camp’(1983) seems the obvious one in particular and just a general enthusiasm for them, how much it meant to watch them. Personally I think I liked ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’ a bit more, overall. I guess there’s the more accessible nature of it, but also I think the nature of what kind of a movie it is was a bit better telegraphed, or rather it translated better. There’s less abstractness, or just vague hintings towards something which for a coherent movie, it gets a bit clunky for me. That abstractness wasn’t really here and I think it was the better for it, the points getting driven more coherently. Also I just liked the look of this, the painted backgrounds make for some really striking imagery. Wished maybe it wasn’t so much trying to be “adjacent” to a slasher. Like there’s one extended sequence of the movie-within-the-movie that went on for a while and felt a bit excessive, for what ultimately felt like just some schlocky fanfare. When it sorta pulls something similar at the end, I felt it just worked alot better. Regardless, I can definitely see it getting a strong cult following though, same as ‘I Saw a the TV Glow’. They almost seem primed towards being the kind of movie that’d earn such a status.

title: Backrooms
my_review: Was a bit middling on this. Really dug all “the backrooms” stuff and was content with the mystery of it, but I felt it just went a bit too far with the explanations and/or content within said backrooms that took a bit away from the allure of what draws people to this idea. Perhaps it’s just not entirely fitting for a full movie, but my idea of the backrooms is a more endless and samey labyrinth of plain rooms with little to no variations. My friend threw out the comparison of the hallways in the show ‘Severance’ which is exactly where my mind drifts towards “the backrooms” being, just seemingly endless hallways that all look the same and then like a random entrance to a room with a goat. Even from personal experience, I always think of this trip for a convention where we stayed in one of those big hotels nearby the convention center and another kid and I were taking the stairs to the lobby because the elevator was out or something, but we got totally lost in the stairway. We went all the way down and opened the door to—a hallway of rooms. We went up several floors to another hallway of rooms. We exhausted ourselves going up and down and even when we tried to go back to our room—we couldn’t find it, just endlessly repeating architecture that started to feel a bit daunting. Possible lack of common sense and observation—most likely, but when I see those pictures of liminal spaces, I think back to those 30min we were totally lost in a hotel with not a sight of another living person(this was daytime too). There’s also some sequencing I had a problem with here. The moment the movie shifts to Renate Reinsve as the protagonist there’s a lot of redundancy because the first third of the movie is ruled by Chiwetel Ejiofor. When she sees the map and we see a flashback of that same map that we obviously already were aware of. Or when she approaches the “door” and the music starts pumping and it’s just sorta flat because we’ve already followed Ejiofor in and out of that doorway, so this big reveal for the same feels very awkward. And then just Reinsve wandering around the backrooms—which again, we’ve already seen Ejiofor do. It’s such an awkward amount of “double dipping” that I don’t know if it was intended or not—it’s so strange. The thought came to mind amidst all of those oddities that I think we should have followed Reinsve from the start and to ‘Apocalypse Now’(1979) this story. That from the rip she’s already curious about what became of Ejiofor and we flashback and move forward, seeing everything from her eyes first and giving more space to Ejiofor showing back up. Cause we leave Ejiofor to follow Reinsve, but she runs into Ejiofor pretty quickly, so if anything the bigger gap between could make it actually feel like he’s been gone for a while. That he could be like Marlon Brando—mythologized by the journey deeper, which is sorta what happens(i.e. the mural), just to a lesser degree here. Cause we’re just doubling up on exploration through the backrooms when really the first journey in is the only key one. That or the doubling up should give the viewer information that makes the second journey more worrisome for whomever’s embarking on it, a lá Justin Long in ‘Barbarian’(2022), finding clues but not knowing any of the context we know. Though Ejiofor is the strongest part of this movie, I feel like we have to have less of him for this to work a bit better. It is a good watch though, very eerie when it’s really working for me and even when it’s not, it’s still very engrossing. One HUGE gripe though. When we’re first introduced to ‘Cap’n Clark’s Ottoman Empire’, I went through a train of thought of “That’s a weird name” into “Wait—brilliant name, he probably sells a lot of ottomans.” But what do I see ounce we see his store—nary an ottoman! I think I clocked two ottomans, possibly three at best within the whole store. I expected ottomans up the wazuh not a common man’s ‘general furniture store’. Hell I don’t even think the backrooms had any ottomans that I can recall, just the woven one in the downstairs room with the doorway. I’d be lying if I said this wasn’t an integral aspect to my enjoyment of this movie.

title: Goody Goody
my_review: Neat premise with some nice baked in building-tension, but I don’t know if it explores it satisfyingly enough for me. Like when I start wanting to poke holes in it because there’s just not much happening—more needs to have happened.

title: Mother Mary
my_review: Didn’t know much going into this, yet I still feel a sense of disappointment on every front I was hoping this to be. Probably just a me thing, but also Lowrey is very hit or miss for me, although I guess there’s just the one “hit” this far, that being ‘The Green Knight’(2021), so maybe I just don’t like Lowrey. This just felt too artsy for its own good. What carries on for two hours, feels like it could be done in one. Honestly it feels like a waste of film, the bulk of this fitting more for an audiobook. There are a few choice moments to see here, like I did quite like the bits where Anne Hathaway’s performing on stage, but the rest… is just yapping. And it’s not even particularly interesting conversation, just a bunch of circling around the subject until it’s time for a random dance break, or flashback. Bah, just not a good watch at all, I’m afraid.
