title: Do Not Enter
my_review: Honestly kinda liked the atmosphere here. Reminds me a bit of ‘Prince Of Darkness’(1987)—that kinda big building/lock-in feel that’s oddly welcoming to me. Though I think with a better story this would have worked better. As it is, there’s not too strong of a narrative and just some barebones horror-plot that isn’t as scary/creepy as the movie treats it.

title: They Will Kill You
my_review: I don’t think you can really knock a movie for being so blatantly influenced by Tarantino since his whole career is blatantly “homaging” other movies. That said though, I did feel a bit’ve a chip on my shoulder coming into this one. Not for the ‘Kill Bill’ness of it all, but moreso the fact that this kinda movie feels like it’s been made several times over at this point and by now I think we’ve probably exhausted how fun it is to see a woman turn around and hunt the hunters. Not like there aren’t a bajillion samey action movies with men, but I feel with the “lowkey badass woman” movies they keep relying on the same beats happening every time—the types of baddies, the gore, the ‘pure of heart vs evil’… and atleast for the time being it’s getting a bit old with how little more they’re bringing to the table. ‘Satanic cult/rich people get chopped down visciously as they bumble around’ isn’t just gonna be a slam dunk every time. Heck, making it ‘Kill Bill’ey was probably the most inspired choice it made—but I don’t know if it committed hard enough beyond ‘making Zazie Beetz The Bride, but with less backstory’. It’s pretty unsatisfying that they hand wave why Beetz is so capable by just saying “she was in prison”, as if that makes her proficient with a sword. For me, committing harder to it would be saying that and then showing some gladiatorial nonsense cause the ‘prison she did time in was a fight pit of the nastiest criminal-fighters around’ or something absurdist to account for the absurdity of how the fight scenes play out. Go full Tarantino and just copy ‘Lady Snowblood’(1973)’s homework. I’m also admittedly just sorta nonplussed by some action choreography these days. They say “It’s ‘Kill Bill’” but then the action just plays out like all the other stunt choreography forward movies do nowadays. That’s more of a “me” nitpick, but there’s a rhythm and repetition to recent stunt choreography that I’m not entirely stoked on and usually lacks something distinguishing to the style to offset it, like the Wuxia-adjacent-style of ‘Kill Bill’ or the realistic sloppiness of ‘Oldboy’(2003)—just anything more than “we’re doing ‘John Wick’ but no guns”. Also a hotter takes “me” thing is I’ve never been on the Zazie Beetz train. I feel like she’s gotten pushed hard in movies(that’s maybe died down a bit recently) and I’ve never been so stoked on her acting or any sort of charisma she has—where-in here I think strong charisma is very much a necessity. This movie just got to the party too late and wore the same thing as everyone else, so in turn it’s gonna be quickly forgotten with any of the others that weren’t able to distinguish themselves enough. Really doesn’t help that this released alongside ‘Ready Ir Not 2: Here I Come’(2026)—which I’m also not terribly stoked on, but I guess I would gravitate more to that. Eugh, humbug.

title: Forbidden Fruits
my_review: Hmmm, really wanted to like this, but it’s not for me. Aside from being smitten with them, Lili Reinhart and especially Victoria Pedretti feel like they could make it big and so I’m always eager to see them finally getting a chance to. So I was looking forward to this, with the additive that its premise sounded unique and possibly alot of fun. But I just don’t think there’s really a movie here. It plays out on this constant hum that just doesn’t really go anywhere, much as you’re waiting for something to kinda start it just keeps that hum going until the last 10min. It’s just one of those “ambient movies” that I’m watching but not really seeing the point out of, things are happening but at the same time nothing feels like it’s happening.  Like it just needs some amount of ‘snap’ to it that breaks up that brrr into story beats.  It also just kinda feels like the story’s holding back too much, or rather doesn’t really build upon itself. Like those last 10min leaning hard into the gorey horror, but there not really being much horror at all, prior to. Or Reinhart kinda just disappears for long spans and the movie kinda feels like it’s waiting for her to return before doing anything else. Pedretti’s fun here, but her character feels like she’s having to shoulder the brunt of this movie which narratively is kinda odd. She’s the comedy, the sex, the character, she’s really just doing alot and that felt a bit odd to me. Like Lola Tung just kinda watches and waits the whole movie and she’s mostly watching Pedretti, but that doesn’t really amount to anything because the story was apparently never really about Pumpkin ingratiating her self with this clique, just her getting close to Apple—so then why so much Cherry? There’s also the strange lesbian undertones here that I’m a lil’ confused as to why they didn’t follow through, or why they even went there. Like at the start, I thought Shipp & Tung were being hinted at, that being why only Fig kept noticing Pumpkin, but that goes nowhere. Or Reinhart & Tung, which we later learn why that when nowhere, because they both knew they were eachother’s sister, yet never told the other that they knew. But the strangest to me was Reinhart & Pedretti, at the end when Pedretti’s calling out Reinhart and she just panics and kisses her—why? This what I mean with the strange undertones, like I feel like that was hinting at Apple being gay, but I also felt like that would play more into her manipulation of Fig & Cherry, this sisterhood/feminist/domineering-control over them to avoid boys in general for her own satisfaction, but I never really got that impression. Reinhart just seems controlling and so that kiss felt so out of nowhere. Wasn’t even like that odd “power play”-type kiss but seemed like she actually wanted Pedretti and this was a panic play to exploit that attraction for control. I dunno, it’s just a strange part of this movie to me, like why not go there, it comes with the witchey territory, it felt organic, yet this movie just saved any sex for only that montage of Pedretti dragging men into dressing rooms to fuck. I feel like there’s something intentionally there and it’s just odd that it’s never really brought into the foreground. It’s not a bad watch and I could see it finding its fans, but just don’t think there’s a lot here to enjoy beyond whatever fan worship there already is in any of these actresses, that or investment in them being altogether here. It feels like there’s something there that it just never took a hold of.

title: Hokum
my_review: It’s pretty solid. I’m apparently in the minority that wasn’t stoked on ‘Oddity’(2024) at all and I was only looking forward to this for mostly Adam Scott. So I got a little wary when my friend wanted to see this because they liked the director, McCarthy and I not knowing the director of this—then looked him up only to see that his last movie I had really dunked on, it being towards the very bottom of my rankings of that year(I even liked ‘Joker: Folie À Deux’(2024) more than it—and I hated that movie). So my anticipation waned a bit with that realization. But no, I actually quite liked this one. It’s a far more mainstream horror, from the story, to the ample amount of jumpscares. But I don’t say that to take away from this, because it does it pretty well, better than most of the non-‘elevated horror’ movies do. There are some parts I feel like nitpicking at(specifically the movie hinging on a particular tool like 5% of the population even owns, let alone takes with them everywhere), or just feel the movie really just dropped the ball on, but ultimately—those are minor issues and this was still a pretty fun movie to see in theaters.

title: Ready or Not 2: Here I Come
my_review: Much as their casts usually rock, I just don’t think I’m a fan of the director duo of Bettinelli-Olpin & Gillett(or perhaps their frequent writer collaborator, Busick—though he impart did ‘Final Destination: Bloodlines’ and that movie was sick). I’m just never really get what so many of their fans seem to get out of their movies. The first ‘Ready Or Not’(2019) is probably the one I like best from them, but even then, I remember the feeling of just kinda smiling and nodding as others gushed while I just never got so into it. The fifth ‘Scream’(2022) they did is maybe them at their worst for me. Again, glowing praises, I was super excited for it—but nope, just started hating it more and more as my hype dwindled more and more. I think the writing’s usually pretty weak, despite how clever it presents itself. It tries to be funny by way of dickish characters being snide, but it just feels more grating than funny. And then I think they stuff too many dynamic characters in that it leads to underutilization and poorer main characters that don’t get to be as quirky. And then I’m just kinda “whelmed” with their filmmaking, it’s not bad but I can’t really find good or bad to say on it. For this one, I felt that there’s a pretty weak setup for this to occur, so much so that it definitely feels thought of after the fact and kinda takes away from the first one’s strong ending. I dunno why they felt the need to add Kathryn Newton’s character, it adds baggage that we really didn’t need for Samara Weaving’s character. I’m actually quite stoked on Newton, but goddamn did I just loathe her character here. Just super petulant and she just keeps griefing Weaving which gets so old so fast. Especially when I kinda felt like a lot of her complaints just seemed kinda self-centered and unreasonable. There was something there with the estrangement at their ages in the present, but Newton keeps harping on when she was a kid and—yeah, what did she expect Weaving to be able to do when she wasn’t much older. The twins were kinda awkward. Sarah Michelle Gellar & Shaun Hatosy are great actors, but their characters were so oddly built on. Hatosy has this strange flip, I felt like. At the beginning he’s kinda squeamish, apprehensive about killing his dad, kinda infantilized by Gellar being more ready to do what he won’t at their father’s orders. But then he turns deranged and twisted having an uncomfortably long sequence of him beating the shit out of Newton. And Gellar’s now afraid of him, what he’ll don’t be were in charge. Like she kept talking so much shit to him the whole movie, so how was she maintaining him? I feel like he should be overcompensating because his family were so demeaning to his inability. Instead he kinda feels totally like Pope(from ‘Animal Kingdom’)—a neurodivergent guy that has a real mean streak  and a violent temper and that doesn’t quite resonate through the whole movie. Gellar having that scene with Weaving felt out of place and kinda felt like they were trying to not make her as evil as everyone else—which again, I don’t think the rest of the movie really show her doing anything to keep him in line. I think the same moments can happen(even Pope had a complex with hurting his abusive parent) but they seem to happen contrary to eachother. Like Gellar can have that same conversation if he is a psycho—OR she can have a slightly different one where she’s just straight lying for a power grab, but both can still end with Hatosy killing her. The rest of the family were fine, kinda more of the same as the first which the family in that were my least favorite part, so similarly I wasn’t that wowed by them. Elijah Wood as this executor of Satan’s will was kinda fun though.  I do think the ending was a bit lame. I kinda side eye a property when they have such a noble ending that don’t let the main character indulge in the vice of power/wealth/entitlement, like finding the buried treasure but only coming out with a singular coin because the main characters can’t have it easy I guess. Especially Weaving & Newton, they like to remind about how lower class they were and Weaving was marrying into a very nice deal—save for the satan stuff. Like why can’t Weaving just give herself a lil’ something atleast, but no, a Tate of power would corrupt her entirely. It’s entertaining enough, but again, I think I’m just not as in love with these guys as much as everyone else is.

title: Pretty Lethal
my_review: Pretty fun movie. It’s ’Green Room’(2015) but replace the punk rock bad with ballerinas and the nazis with vaguely Eastern European gangsters.  For as reputable and good as the action was in it, I feel like this movie is the one with more creativity with idea of “killer ballerinas” than ‘From The World Of John Wick: Ballerina’(2025)(Is that what they’re calling it now?). The choreography and imagination of how you’d “dance to kill” is this movie’s strongest aspect. It does get a bit gritty with the fight scenes, but for the most part it’s pretty schlocky with it and that works well enough for me. That said though, I do think there’s alot of weird kinks in here. Kinks in the actual foundation of the movie and just odd moments that feel like rookie mistakes to make it out of the editor’s room. It’s the writing that’s mostly ‘off’ to me. The premise is good, but Uma Thurman’s role in it is weird and kinda untapped potential. Doesn’t really make any sense why she’d so readily want to kill the ballerinas when her ulterior motive is revealed to be revenge for her leg. She feels great sympathy and compassion for the ballerinas, yet it’s her who orders all the men to hunt them down, aswell as just not caring if they live or not. She could just be villainous, but I think the more interesting play would be her using the ballerinas but not actively trying to get them killed. Cause the gangster son’s guys are the first to try and kill them, but after that Thurman is the one to order everyone else to go and kill them—which could just as well have also been the son and not make Thurman’s character this flippantly sympathetic revenger that gets to “save” the ballerinas while also being a big reason why they’re almost killed for the whole movie. Then there’s also just weird little moments that aren’t big enough to really talk too much on, but still really bothered me unnecessarily and I have to point out. • When they’re doing the pep talk to go fight their way out, Apatow is muttering “We have to get out of here…” and Ziegler snaps at her to ‘stop that’ and —‘just saying that isn’t doing anything good because— we have to get out of here.” Like what? The scene falls flat immediately and it’s just so awkward and rewatching it—I don’t think it’s for comedy either. • There’s also a minor part that bugged me where Apatow realizes no one else was thinking about her sister and they all look kinda guilty about it and Condor makes an unnecessarily mean comment about it and Ziegler snaps back to “stop being so selfish”. But like—she wasn’t being selfish, just very cruel and her, Condor and Avantika all seemed guilty seconds earlier—guilty of what actually seemed selfish. It’s just one small bit, but it really bothered me, like they had a line where that made sense and just callously edited it out or cut in a different take with a new snide comment and it felt like someone should have caught that • Also a minor complaint—why do they not urgently tell Simmons that they’re in survival mode. The sisters bicker and they even drag her out before she tells her they’re in danger. Like goddamn, does she even know that their teacher got shot in cold blood and these gangsters are hunting them in order to handle the problem?  These all feel like problems with the writing or problems with rewriting and not proof-reading. They feel like a bunch of tiny mistakes that just piled up for me. It’s nitpicking, but also I feel like they're just too easily caught to be problems. Writing aside, this is a decent watch. The girls have a fun dynamic and there’s not too much frustration in their coming to terms with their situation—something that most thrillers/horrors are annoyingly prone to doing(as an aside, I couldn’t help but wonder though if they wanted Sophie Thatcher as ‘Bones’, cause that character seemed so in her wheelhouse). It could have used a once over, but it’s still pretty solid.

title: The Bride!
my_review:
Maggie Gyllenhaal seems to want to skip the part of having written something ‘remarkable and full of the clever feminist themes’ and instead seems to want to just skip to the part where we all agree that that’s exactly what she’s done here.

Big whiff, if only upheld by how audacious it is as a passion project. Really let down by this.

title: Scream 7
my_review: I kinda liked it? I saw such a wave of poor reviews and tepid responses to this movie and that kinda deflated my looking forward to it, but I don’t quite see why it’s getting dogpiled on so much. It’s not perfect, but it did miss alot of the issues I had with the last two and just the added perk of Sidney being back. I do have one idea about why the dogpile—I don’t wanna discredit all criticism some might have, but I think it’s fairly there, but the ‘very public firing of Melissa Barrera’ and ‘dipping of Jenna Ortega’ both left a bad taste in people’s mouths. In part cause Barrera voiced support of an injustice and got shafted for it and also that what followed was the creatives that had currently held the reins also left in solidarity. Ortega also left soon after, though I’m not entirely certain for moral reasons, but possibly just the ship seeming to sink and she was already too big for what her part was. They all had their fans and so I think this had mud to drive out of at the start and then just unenthusiastic response regardless if it got out of the mud or not. That said—I don’t really have that attachment to any of the new(now old)-guard. I was hyped as hell when 5 came out but I just did not like it at all. I felt their interpretation of the ‘Scream’ series was tedious and overly masturbatory. It leaned into what I felt were low points in the series and leaned them into even lower points. The whole “Billy Loomis birthright” nonsense was from leftfield and unnecessary and the more they tried explaining themselves in constant meta-nagging, the worse the movie got. It created a circle of characters(the “core four”) and kept cheaply “killing” them only to show up at the end(that’s something the originals also faltered in, but it felt egregious in the last two—or maybe I was just already done with it). Ghostface was now like a possession into a super killer, regardless of size—fuckin’ 5’3” Mikey Madison overpowering and lifting a full grown man cause she’s wearing the costume. The cloak and dagger murdering turned into Michael Meyers-like boldness in brazenly crashing in on moments where they could have easily been overpowered like a bodega full of people or an apartment full of survivors(not the subway with everyone dressed up, that was good, that’s what I wanted). And then—honestly, Melissa Barrera is just not nearly as good an actress as her cult following would have you believe. Political beliefs aside, she’s a weak point in most movies I’ve seen with her. Especially in movies full of good actors that kinda do circles around her. Then the movie would just double down on her and make it meta how people dislike her as they make a martyr out of Barrera and her character. It’s mean to say, but I kinda just feel bad that she’s constantly put in the leading seat and then someone big Ortega has to be second fiddle to her. I’m probably terrible for kinda being relieved when they left(were fired), but boy I hated ‘ScreVm’(2022) and was felt ‘Scream VI’(2023) was better, but only as good as ‘Scream 3(2000)—which used to easily be the worst one. So I’m already on a different page from where I think alot of people are coming from. Not only the eagerness for different creatives, but that people actually quite liked the last two. Though I think this series is polarizing in general cause people shit on ‘Scre4m’(2011) and that to me was the second best movie in the franchise. But yeah, I didn’t see alot I didn’t like with this one. I’m not obsessed with Sidney Prescott having to be the center of this universe—though each movie treats her as such, but she is my favorite scream-queen and I like getting to see her kick ass again(goddamn I loved her stabbing the fuck outta Anna Camp). Somehow returning to her feels less hamfisted than the whole “daughter of Billy Loomis”-destiny nonsense. They tried doing that to Sidney in 3 and it was terrible. Her daughter is a bit daft though—zero awareness of herself, though that kinda seems plot relevant. I liked Joel McHale as the husband though, albeit he does get beat up each time and it’s wild that he lived through that attack after what—5–7hrs, that’s points against this since it seemed so definitive to then not be. But I liked that he also was 100% with Sidney, she calls and says “killer” and he comes running without the “calm down, you’re being crazy…”  For the other returnees, I liked how they fit in here, not too dominant but fun to see. Like Gale’s pretty toned down here, but her always being roped in is kinda what helped the series get old as she’s adjacent-final girl. This was also the first time I actually liked the twins. Chad was actually better defined in the last one, but god, Mindy’s an abonoxious character in 5 & 6. Here they were used just enough. I take that as this movie not overloading the “meta”-ness to try and sound smart. It’s cute that they’re also paired with Gale. It was a lil’ odd how everyone relocates to New York in the last one, so this gives a clear in for why they show up. Though, additional knocks cause they both get attacked and once again both make it after—fainting from the stabs and slashes? It weird that Ghostface just leaves them to go brutalize the two kids. And that’s a bit of another knock, the new cast is pretty underutilized. Tatum is a shithead for most of this and gets to be front and center, but everyone else kinda exists in the background until they’re yanked in to be killed. They’re also pretty stupid, like the weirdo, Lucas, running in to be a hero(?) and popping out stabbed or the boyfriend making deepfakes of himself as the killer—like what? The two close friends of Tatum hardly do much, one dying before really getting to do much and the other not doing much with Tatum. I think it’s from a weird juggling act of trying to make Tatum to spiritual/literal successor and still wanting Neve Campbell to be front and center, so it’s just a weird hot and coldness of new characters being utilized or not.  Like the revealed killers are super underutilized, Anna Camp and…Ethan Embry from that one scene. It became pretty obvious to me that They were the killers early on and that kinda ruins the reveal. I think mostly cause there’s no real localization of characters/suspects, they’re all sprawled out so you know more concretely that it’s someone never on screen or never at a place of importance. Also doesn’t help that they’re both two bigger names given real bit parts here. Like I’ve hardly seen Anna Camp—ofcourse it’s gonna be her / oh it’s a rough loonking Ethan Embry working at the mental institute the mystery killer’s from ofcourse it’s him. What was even stranger is there’s some dynamic going on there between them that seemed like it was going to turn into something, her chastising him for interjecting on her big moment, but Embry’s killed before getting to do anything, like even explain his “why”. Also Camp’s monologue’s not terribly good—not her, but the explanation for why she went crazy? Like she’s full wacko and even killed her own son and it’s kinda just “Oh yeah—whatever, anyways, back to you being my hero…” Almost feel like Camp should have been the secret Ghostface reveal, akin to Emma Roberts in ‘Scr4m’. Mayhaps she gets these willing goons to be the Ghostfaces terrorizing Sidney in order to reignite Sidney’s heroism…? I dunno, it felt odd how much she praises Sidney and that turning into her wanting to kill Sidney—all the other AI nonsense could have just been Embry’s motive, or whatever. But yeah, they’re pretty weak reveals. Will give props though, I’ve been waiting for so long for the killer to get got in the middle of the movie which this does. Maybe not to the extent I’d’ve Hoped though, cause like I always thought an interesting dynamic is a killer whose plans aren’t going well. Like if one half of the killer duo gets arrested or killed, what becomes of the still hidden one? That said, I felt like the kills in here were sick. The first one with Jimmy Tatro getting the knife in the brain was an awesome start and I felt like they kept delivering after that. I will say though, Ghostface does do a few things that I can’t see them being a toss up being Camp or Embry which is a problem I had with 5 & 6. Mostly cause I’m pretty sure Camp is the one that kills her own son and the way Ghostface picks him up I don’t see camp doing. Same with overpowering Joel McHale or any other of the tall muscular guys. Embry and the crazy guy look sturdy, so they easily make sense, but not Camp. Especially when Anna Camp isn’t onscreen so you have to assume she’s Ghostfacing. Like ‘Scream 2’(1997) I have issues with their killers, but I can also figure that Olyphant does most of it and the ones I think Laurie Metcalf can do—they seem plausible. I guess it’s unavoidable that Ghostface empowers the killers, but I still appreciate it when you’re not left wondering how the hell some of it works logistically when they don’t do things that would make sense for a shorter killer to do. Partly why Stu and Billy work so well, because you can believe either could do the killing. Like they’re literally two whole Ghostfaces. Though it’s not that bad here, I’m probably nitpicking—it’s a lil’ bad, but not that bad. Just yesterday I saw some Reddit thread and someone ranked the ‘Scream’ movies like “1>6>4>2>5>3>7” and honestly I don’t see how this is possibly that bad. I think where this falters—it’s not “fuck this 1⭐️ it is”-bad yet it seems to attract that response so much. This was very watchable and maybe it’s cause it’s the first I caught in theaters, but the thrills were thrilling, like as entertainment it works and inoffensibly so. Like I can see people liking 5 & 6, but they’re both so notably distinct in the way that they are so I would think it’s also understandable how some wouldn’t like them. But this is just pretty “okay” at the least I’d think. Even if you were to put 5 & 6 towards the front—it’s still way better than 3. I might put it at or behind 2 for myself, middle of the back(1>4>2/7>6>3>5)

title: Psycho Killer
my_review: Kinda shocking how good this looks for how mediocre it is as a movie. Could be off base, but this feels like someone’s direct “homage” to ‘Longlegs’(2024). So much of the aesthetic and story(whatever story there might be) seems to “borrow” heavily from that thriller. But there just no actual movie here, just burps of a story and moody shots and an extremely uninteresting slasher.  I came for Georgina Campbell, but my goodness did she lead me into a trap. Ye be warned—this ain’t it.

title: The Dreadful
my_review: You shouldn’t judge a book entirely by its cover, but you should make exceptions when they’re obvious. Compare this movie’s poster to the movie it’s remaking’s—‘Onibaba’(1964). That about sums this movie up.

title: Twisted
my_review: Watched this on the whim of seeing Djimon Hounsou on the poster, so I didn’t really know what to expect. I think there’s something here, but it feels like didn’t quite think it’d get as far as it did and it just starts improvising a whole movie out of some general outline. Like it starts decently I feel like—lesbian con artist(duo?) and then it does something I’m always a huge fan of which is “bad meets evil” with a crazy neurosurgeon. But that’s about where I think it doesn’t have much else. Our girl spends so much time flailing and screaming—oddly lunging like a rabid animal and Hounsou just sorta does nothing until he’s doing everything. There’s a neat bit with the girlfriend catching onto a well laid clue and she enters the mix and that just doesn’t really go anywhere interesting, just adds to the body count while our girl just screams and flails some more. Neal McDonough is here to and then he’s not. And then I think the only other thing planned was Alicia Witt killing Hounsou in a twisted(🥁) fashion. Like there’s a good story here, this just never found it, kinda just settling for schlock of a straight to streaming movie. I think of ‘Fresh’(2022) or ‘Perfection’(2018) and they’re about on this movie’s wavelength, but they had a better idea of what to do with themselves. Will say, an odd thing I noticed with this story is the similarities with ‘Get Out’(2017). And it’s interesting that this ends up a sorta inverse with the Black man imprisoning White people in bodies through brain surgery. Could just be some straws grasped from similarities, but it is interesting—the italics feel a little more charged than I intend, so to say it might be worth noting. I do think the direction should be noted here. There is some flair which I think is always welcome, even though it’s sometimes… a choice. Like the sharp tilt they kept doing or the wild lighting at the end, but also the strange compositing of picture-in-picture angles of Hounsou dying. But it’s a fun movie night. Certainly wouldn’t be a winner pick, but it’s alright for what it is.

title: The Strangers: Chapter 3
my_review: Three for three, that’s a pretty hard accomplishment.

title: Iron Lung
my_review: I bought the game when it recently when on sale I assume for this movie’s release and I planned on playing it first before watching. But I got some bug that made it so it didn’t count one of the spots I surveyed and it was already so far back and I kept progressing normally that I thought I’d be fine but nope, just sorta soft locked myself at what I feel was the big payoff. Admittedly I didn’t try too terribly hard to get through it, cause the game itself is kinda frustrating to engage with, being very tedious to progress and instant loss at the hint of a bump in a wall(laughable that this movie says the “ship” can tank the hit when every bump sent me straight to the starting screen). I was bemused with it though, but for full disclosure, I didn’t even finish to be able to faithfully compare, even forgot to just look the ending up and after watching I’m thinking back to if I missed quite a bit of interaction with the game from just not fucking around enough. That preamble through, it’s alright. Admittedly only know of Markiplier through the osmosis of YouTube culture, I’ve never seen anything of his, all I know is he’s got a real nice voice, all that to say: I’m not swayed by any fandom of his nor of this game. I say this not derogatorily(atleast not so much so), but this movie very much feels like a “YouTube”-movie. A very well produced “YT”-movie, but still very much is one. By that I mean it feels very confident and self-assured in what it wants to be—atleast from my perspective, this feels like very few compromises were made for this passion project to be made how Markiplier wanted it to be made. But what I also mean by “YT”-movie, is that alongside all that, it feels pretty unremarkable, to be blunt. Very safe and retraced steps made, an emulation of what works and its effect is a product that feels competent, but lacking any extraneous style and voice, from the script, to the look and just the general story, it all feels very familiar. The lack of bold strokes do make this feel a bit more boorish than it probably is. That “uncompromised vision” feeling ‘too whole’ and probably in need of some compromising choices from either more experienced voices or just external feedback willing to be critical. Like the runtime is a big offender here—at most this is a 90min movie, not a 2hr long one. The game itself is only around the 1hr–1.5hr mark and there’s even a lot of dead space that can be filled with something(worth noting the game does thrive on this “dead air” of activity, building more to the jumpscares of the photographs). It going so long feels like a telltale indicator of being too precious about everything here, when there’s clear fat to be trimmed and clear unwanted sluggish pacing. In turn I just never quite got so caught up in the “adrenaline” of the movie, it just failing to create the desperation and urgency needed. Also could have just used a bit more deviation from the game. A lot of the mundanity works quite well for the game, but I don’t think that translates so 1:1 for a whole movie. A neat aspect that could’ve gone more into is him mapping things out or just the general tin can nature of this sub and the need to hotfix random problems. Actually an issue I had that the game did somewhat better was this not feeling like a submarine at all. For one, they hardly call it a sub(“ship”), but for another, there feels like no pressure happening in this under blood-sea adventure. All the blood leaks in, maybe once did it squirt in, but a classic sub trope for me is the high pressure spurts of water spewing in—imagining that, but with blood feels like such a missed opportunity and a bit of a waste of the setting. In general you don’t really feel any true sense of this guy being in a “death sentence”, tons of blood on top of him ensuring he has nowhere to go. Often it actually just feels like he’s on a boat if anything, all the leaks just sorta seeping in rather than burst in. I feel like those tweets would’ve gone a long way with the general tensity it wants to ramp up towards, especially by the end. I started thinking back to Damien Chazelle’s tepid Neil Armstrong movie, ‘First Man’(2018) and though the movie itself had a lot of issues, it’s one of the few movies I feel like accurately showcase how goddamn terrifying and stupid humans were to try and go to the moon with that level of tech. Equipment loosely rattling, flimsy material, high velocity movements with zero room for error—that’s something I feel could’ve been played with here and instead it ends up feeling like Markiplier’s stuck in an escape room that occasionally floods with blood. I liked it more than this probably seems, but it really does just feel super safe, ultimately. Like I made a funny face when the credits rolled and the flashed “ADRENALINE BY:…” and I had to see if that meant score and yup—score and sound. The funny reaction being from me thinking throughout how blasé this music felt. I’m feeling a bit pedantic and overly scrutinizing, but this really did just feel too ‘by the numbers’ and not freehanded. The idea is unique and I can see why Markiplier was so taken to it for a movie, but I guess it just feels like there wasn’t much of a vision beyond plainly making it a movie and in turn adding “common movie things” do accomplish that, which feels like the wrong way to tackle an adaptation.

title: Buddy
my_review:
I was glad when this got into the weird lore-baitey stuff. Not that I in particular like it, but cause I feel like if you're harking to internet culture phenomena like 'Don't Hug Me, I'm Scared'(or even 'Too Many Cooks'(2014)), the rabbithole of theories and drawn out lore and fan debates feels like a package deal at this point. Like 'The Backrooms'(2026) or 'Five Nights At Freddy's'(2023) might be more extreme cases of that and atleast for me, hindering to general enjoyment, but I feel you can't deny that the fans of them just eat it up whenever some deep cut is made.

That said, it's alright. Maybe lacks some real payoff, atleast for me. In that regard it feels similar to Casper Kelly's 'Too Many Cooks', this maybe having been stronger as a short than a feature, cause I don't know if it's utilizing its "featureness" to up the ante enough. Somewhat a similar issue to what I had with 'The Backrooms', it feeling like it was building towards something big and then fizzling out cause the real moment was "all dat juicy lore referencing". That's not quite what's happening here, but at the same time I felt like this was too quick to nip something that would've been interesting. 

Like for me, Buddy kills too fast sometimes and in the same vein, how inactive side characters are. Like Wade was a good character done in too fast(albeit I liked the somewhat subtle joke of the one Black kid being replaced by another Black kid as if to maintain the token status on the show). Or Cristin Milioti, I thought her involvement would lead to way more than her just sacrificing herself for a girl she, mere minutes prior to, remembered was her daughter. Also kinda wished the other puppets or adult characters did anything of note, they were weirdly involved yet mostly bystanders for the whole while and it felt a bit uneven in their writing in that regard.

It's a fun horror though. Can't say I was so wowed with it, but it was a good watch.

title: Cold Storage
my_review: Very uneven movie. There’s alot of weird story beats, lack of payoff and a weird sense of a blockbuster story packaged in something that looks very minimal and lower budget. But it also has pretty good main characters and decent enough character arcs. So yeah, it just feels very ‘uneven’. Georgina Campbell and Joe Keery really are the heart of this—and that’s kinda the problem. This wants to have some comedic ‘Resident Evil 2’-like story, but it makes so much of it Campbell & Keery’s chemistry together as they slowly uncover the “zombie plot” of the movie. But it’s not really a rom-com-zom movie, it’s just a zom-com, so it doesn’t really go too far into their budding romance, yet it still monopolizes the movie so much. I thought it’d turn into some team of misfits fighting zombies, but it’s just some misfits kinda just going up and going down until they’re ready to leave. Like Vanessa Redgrave has a literal Chekhov’s Gun and she uses it, but immediately is ushered out of the movie, no problem(never even really interacting with Neeson, which is a missed opportunity since they’re family). It’s trying way too much all at once while trying to have some originality but it just makes such an awkwardly paced movie. There’s not really stakes either aside from the safety of the main characters which is rarely in jeopardy. This is a fast acting fungus infection and it stays localized in the middle of nowhere? It infected a dude with a car pretty fast, so why would it stay so localized in the middle of nowhere. We see the deer stinger, but that doesn’t feel too canonical, but rather just a cheeky ending with a question mark. It infects several people—people with guns, but they’re hardly threatening as the fungus is very inconsistent on mutating organic bombs and spitters. Most of the infected are people just acting very mild mannered or panicky. There’s also the high ranking officer(general?) that doesn’t appreciate the weight of Neeson’s backstory and worry, but aside from catching the soldier on the phone, he’s such a nonthreat of an ignorant antagonist that’d typically be the guy unknowingly preventing the good guys from saving the day. The dumb boss too. Typically his ignorance and bullheaded attitude would ensure karmic blowback, but he almost walks out, only deciding to be a dick after seeing the gravity of the situation and getting shot by characters who really had nothing to do with him. I also had some issue with the structure of this. The prologue both Bacon is kinda underwhelming and weirdly executed. For one, they make little effort to mask the age of Neeson and Manville, so I was wondering how Neeson was going to meetup with the other people on the poster cause—he looks about the same as he does later. It’s also odd how few people show up when Bacon already knows pretty distinctly that a whole town has basically gone radio silent. Also the fungus burning through her shoe kinda ruins the movie’s logic as the extent of how capable this fungus is. It burns through to the soles of shoes but it never tries again in the movie, mostly just infecting like normal. Maybe the exe had it happen to him, I admittedly missed how he got infected, but just as well assumed the cat did it. Which is the other issue, I don’t really see a point to the nonlinear story telling. We see the cat obviously infected and it is somewhat puzzling, but not enough for a twenty minute later cutaway sequence about how the cat got infected, that also felt inconsistent cause the roach walks right past Vanessa Redgrave. I kinda feel like the movie could have just played out from mostly Campbell & Keery’s POV without the fungus getting a montage for the “how’s & why’s”—or rather, I want that prologue to be more impactful than [currently] nominally famous Sosie Bacon being the surprise death at the beginning and that being it. Ultimately, it is actually pretty enjoyable. Campbell & Keery are the ones I really came into this for and again, they’re the best part of it. Much as I dislike the phrase, I think it’s apt here, but it’s probably better to shut your brain off for this. Not because it’s an action movie/dumb fun—which is when people mostly use the term—but cause there’s alot this doesn’t do well with. I feel this has ambitions of being a bigger movie, but this should have been treated as a smaller and more intimate movie, a lá something like RE2(without Mr. X and other supercreatures). But for what it turned out, it’s not a bad watch really.

title: Send Help
my_review: I so very enjoyed watching this. This is just movies at their “funnest”. It’s exceptional at what it wants to be and what that is is a killer movie for movie night. I was worried coming into this—not really catching the trailer, that this would be retracing the steps of ‘Triangle Of Sadness’(2022) from only four years ago. Boiling down to the dynamic of the ‘lesser’ person being in a situation where they thrive and their ‘superiors’ must adapt to the new dynamic. And yes this movie does turn into that same dynamic—even with the additive of the newly empowered character finding out they’re a jaunt away from civilization and that frightens them into becoming selfish and evil—but this movie’s also so much more. It’s ’Misery’(1990) on an island, it’s a fun comedy, it’s a very tense thriller and it’s just a damn good time. But even more to me is I feel like there’s alot under the hood that really helps it feel it’s of its own self, rather than being so derivative of many other survival scenarios. The idea of a “loser” and frumpish Rachel McAdams feels like a oxymoron, yet here she is as a bottom feeder of the chain to Dylan O’Brien’s nepo-granted ‘apex predator’-position on said food chain. When they get stranded the chain is immediately broken into McAdams now thriving and O’Brien now squirming. O’Brien has to now rely on McAdams to do everything for him cause he can’t do it himself—but that’s not really a change in their dynamic. McAdams already did everything for the company, but they either didn’t care or her efforts were claimed by others. This isn’t much different from ‘Triangle Of Sadness’, there the almost unseen(if I recall correctly) character of the lowest tier of workers on the cruise ship is now made the provider and defacto leader because nobody can really dispute that she has all the power on the island. Where I do think it differs is how goddamn resistant O’Brien is to this dynamic. McAdams is now the defacto leader but O’Brien hates that notion and never concedes to it. O’Brien throughout the whole movie hates McAdams’ Linda Liddle. He hates the sight of her when he inherits his father’s head position—retching at how repugnant she is and her admittedly slobbish manners with the tuna sandwich. He joins—or rather welcomes his preferred underlings to mock her with him. When the guy pulls up her ‘Survivor’ audition tape, they can’t stop laughing at a pretty innocuous promotional video because she’s featured in it trying to be “fun”. You’d think they’d stop when McAdams finally breaks concentration to hear their laughter but when she looks and sees what their laughing at—O’Brien turned to look right at her, in the eyes to laugh at her. When he’s first awoken on the island he’s still repulsed by her, caring very little for whatever efforts she’s made to make him comfortable and heal him. It’s not until McAdams cuts him off that he comes groveling to her, realizing she was the only one surviving for him. He comes around and becomes more of a partner in their survival. This lasts a good bit as McAdams teaches him and even her island hotness becomes more undeniable. But this is a farce, O’Brien still has resented her and positions her(I think for the second time) so he can make a getaway with his own raft—flipping her off while doing so. I don’t think there’s ever a moment where O’Brien doesn’t resent McAdams being on top. They do bond—him revealing his abusive mother(might be important later) and even saving her from falling off the cliff, but I don’t think this is ever because he likes McAdams. We later see him being extremely manipulative towards McAdams—almost succeeding in getting in close just to kill her, so him revealing personal things about himself is almost certainly somewhat a ploy, same as all his longing looks of attraction he gives or notices McAdams giving. And I think his saving of her from the cliff is only because he still has use for her—to learn enough that he can escape. My friend and I had a pretty lengthy debate after the movie, about what are the ethics of McAdams getting a happy ending after sabotaging their rescue and killing three people for selfish reasons. My friend argued that her sabotaging a rescue was irredeemable and that we know that she’s keeping him hostage, basically and trying to manipulate him—a lá Misery/Annie Wilkes. But for me, I rooted for McAdams the whole way through and I wondered why that was. Ultimately they’re both bad people—atleast when given power, but where it gets a lil’ wonky and what my friend really argued for was—the vibes are there. We the audience know that McAdams is miserying him and thus there’s just the weird vibes that O’Brien can and does seem to pick up on throughout. McAdams won’t let him use the “found” knife. She tells him to stay away from one spot of the island. She starts to lust after him. Plus, O’Brien has a history of a maternal figure abusing him, something McAdams both acts as and happens to be decently older than O’Brien. The vibes are totally there. Where I differ on that is, just because we know O’Brien is right to distrust and run from her, doesn’t make O’Brien himself right in doing so. O’Brien’s motives aren’t from just vibes, they’re from resentment and I think O’Brien’s rottenness earns him the karmic forces that be to suffer him through McAdams. O’Brien was going to ruin McAdams life by firing her. He first denied her the job she earned and his father promised her and when confronted with that fact he plotted to exploit her again just for this business trip, firing her after when he no longer had use for her. He has the same mentality on the island, all that bonding being another way to exploit her so he can learn enough to build a raft and ditch her. He hates that McAdams has all the power in this dynamic. He only wants to exploit her for his own benefit and any time she seems to want to “exploit him”—or rather gain something beneficial from him for her hard work—he seems to give just enough so that he can continue to exploit her, such as letting her bond while he plots an escape from her. McAdams might be Misery, but O’Brien is Justin Long in ‘Barbarian’(2022). I think this dynamic is what really sets this movie apart. That McAdams tries to be the villain, such as O’Brien is in the office, but O’Brien can’t stand to let her. That a woman can’t exploit a man for personal gratification because the man can’t stand the turned tables. All McAdams really seems to want is O’Brien to not see her as a detestable loser. She’s not a malicious captor, she’s kind and lighthearted the entire time. Yes, O’Brien does suggest more proactive measures to get maybe rescued only to be shot down by McAdams, but from what we see—McAdams never antagonistically forbids him from doing so himself. He secretly builds a raft for no reason other than he hates McAdams. McAdams never demolishes his builds or scolds him for trying, he just does so with the intent of damning her to isolation on the island. Yes, he is a prisoner and McAdams does even kill to make that so, but he is not a prisoner in the same way we perceive him as. We know McAdams is doing everything to keep him there, but he wants to escape because he just can’t stand to not have power and especially to not have McAdams have power over him. He was never authentic because he never wanted to be with McAdams. That could stem from his childhood of abuse, but I think it’s also just that he only values McAdams for what she can give him and when he think he doesn’t need her, he’d willfully screw her over. Oddly most damning is he’s so friggin’ selfish that when he makes his getaway—he notably steals McAdams personalized cup. There’s little use for just a cup and McAdams seemed to have made quite a few bamboo receptacles, but O’Brien’s such a terrible person that he’d even steal that. So I believe O’Brien ‘—gets what he fuckin’ deserved’ by the end. McAdams is wrong for killing to innocent people, but I don’t think she’s wrong for killing O’Brien. All that out of the way, both Rachel McAdams and Dylan O’Brien are great here. McAdams is always a gem and seeing her as such a layered villain is a treat. O’Brien has slowly crept into becoming quite the actor—last year having one of my favorite performances in ‘Twinless’(2025) and he really sells this deplorable human of Bradley Preston. His scoffs and retches at McAdams get a giggle but they’re also so essential to these characters’ dynamic.  I really do just love how ‘in-your-face’ this movie is with moments. Such as the boar hunt being so visceral and gross, or the dead fiancé’s hand protruding from the ground to perfectly showcase the fat diamond ring she had on. But at the same time there’s just so many subtleties that carry the same overt meaning, but I feel like they’re so expertly sprinkled in. Such as how I’ve stated O’Brien’s selfishness and willingness to take from McAdams, a small but poignant moment just kinda thrown in there is when O’Brien grovels while McAdams is dining on a ridiculously lavish meal and she finally lets him join her—giving him his own tray, he just starts housing the food and looks at her looking away and steals a slice of papaya from her tray while continuing to house his own. There’s something about the campiness that Sam Raimi operates in that just works so much where I feel like it shouldn’t. Obvious exposition, gratuitous character traits’n motives, overtly on the nose story beats, insanely gross and violent insanity… like these are the things other directors can be knocked for. There’s so much that feels rudimentary in terms of filmmaking, but at the same time it’s also pure? I feel Raimi is of a class of directors(I’d lump with Lynch & Shyamalan) who for better or worse operate at such an basic level of filmmaking, but it’s the way they make it work for their storytelling that sets them apart—again, for better or worse. It’s not “so bad it’s good”, but rather “so blatant it’s everything”. He really utilizes the visual medium and it’s both just so entertaining and digestible for I think anyone to appreciate the nuance of the camp. Great movie. Great performances. Great gore. Great story. Just a damn good time with a movie.

title: 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple
my_review: I liked this. Not a bad sequel by any means—but not even close to its predecessor, I feel like. ‘28 Years Later’(2025) was a ‘weird downright experimental’-film, while this one is much more straightforward and that comes with some good and some bad. Like there’s alot I don’t think worked with the last one, but that’s also alot of its charm I find in it. I believe it’s that weirdness that breathes life into this strange “zombie”-evolved world. That the most beautiful thing you’ve seen is a orange man process a dying mother so her son can have closure and growth by taking her fresh skull to the top of a mountain of skulls—that’s fuckin’ weird, but it’s one of the greatest things I’ve seen in film. This movie strips down this world a bit to a more conventional tone and I think that does take out alot of the oddities that riddle the previous one and somehow it doesn’t make this one hit as hard. But I think alot of that’s also the story. This one has a bridge to build and the materials it was given aren’t necessarily as brilliant as the last one’s. Jimmy dominates this movie and I don’t think that’s really a good thing. Jimmy and his Jimmies spend most of the movie just terrorizing people, barely having a sliver of reason to it, it’s just what they do—because they’re crazy and Satanic. The eccentric Jimmy is a villain cliché that feels so tired nowadays. From that era of the type of villain that ruled the peak of the XBOX360 era, with your Handsome Jack’s & Vaas’s… Though I love some of them, that type of villain had its moment and I think I’m kinda over ‘em? Atleast—maybe I’m just over the shallow ones. Jimmy just doesn’t do it for me—none of the Jimmies do. We hardly see much of how they exist, only getting to see how they torment and that’s just not so captivating to me. Jimmy himself just doesn’t feel like as amazing a character. Not O’Connell’s fault at all, I just don’t think there’s much for him to play with. There’s too much time skinning people and fighting to the death and not enough of Jimmy being a cult leader. He does it while they skin and fight to the death, but it doesn’t feel so impressionable. As a comparison, I don’t think most agree with(and I certainly don’t back this statement up so much as I dipped shortly after this introduction), but ‘The Walking Dead’s introduction to Neagan I feel is comparable to what Jimmy gets to work with and for my money, Neagan leaves so much more of an impression than Jimmy does with less time. Jimmy does have his moment though and it is of of the best parts of the movie, but for being the bulk of this, I think it’s a big miss for this movie not to nail him in a spectacular way. Who doesn’t dominate this movie, is poor Spike. Spike takes a huge backseat in this movie and it’s kinda the worst thing this movie could do. The last move had such a strong theme of ‘losing boyish innocence’—really that supplanting the whole “zombie horror”-side of this series. I tried looking out for it here, but I don’t think there’s much of any strong themes and that’s really unfortunate. Perhaps this was supposed to be another factor of Spike’s story, but it feels like a regression. By the end of the last movie, Spike willfully decides to not return to the safety of the village and to venture out on his own because he’d become disillusioned with his father and what it means to be an adult. And so Spike getting forced into this cult and digressing into a scared boy—that feels like a big step back. Sure, Spike isn’t an adult with full maturity, but he’s just so helpless here. A moment that struck my friend and I quite a bit was the woman from the group they filleted alive, when she attacks and makes a run for it, Spike catches up with her and instead of killing her, he begs her to take him—why? Like why does Spike need her to take him? Lil’ dude was surviving fine in his own, so in that regard he doesn’t need her. But the threat of the Jimmies chasing him is going to happen regardless of if he’s with the woman or not. I think he basically even tries to leave on his own later—and it just makes that one scene feel so strange. Strange in the context of both movies. Like in my mind, Spike wouldn’t be begging, Spike would just try to be helping. For him to beg and the woman to distrust him and strand him with the Jimmies—it’s just a bit hamfisted. She can still distrust him and still strand him with the Jimmies, but the way that scene played out rubs me so wrong—not in the offended way, but just narratively. Spike being a wallflower and given no agency in this movie deeply upsets the story for me. It doesn’t make sense and it’s just strange, especially when you look at what they did do and it’s just the Jimmy nonsense. The other thief of Spike’s story—and so so oddly most other movies, is Erin Kellyman/‘s character. I don’t know what godlike agent she has to inject her into such an acclaimed array of roles with such prominence, but she seems to just show and show up with a spotlight. Kellyman’s “Jimmy Ink” kinda steals what would be Spike’s agency, I feel like. She’s seemingly the oldest of the Jimmies and thus, the one that questions Jimmy the most. So we spend a good bit of time with her and how she’s ‘not like the other Jimmies’, cause she feels protective of the helpless Spike. Like she buys into Jimmy’s bullshit, but she’s also cool enough to be a good person—even though I feel those ideas are at odds with eachother based on what we see it takes for someone to be a Jimmy. I dunno if I just feel biased against her character, or just cause I feel like this is the sort of thing I get alot with Kellyman’s roles. There’s some amount of “main character”-twinge added to each one and it really sticks out I feel like cause it never feels so organic. Like how Spike’s regression feels odd, ‘Jimmy Ink’s prominence feels odd. I don’t think the character doesn’t have a place here, but my goodness if feels like the character is molded for Kellyman rather than the Kellyman molding herself into the role. I don’t think she has and hand in it, but it feels like creatives like to keep using her in the same way and it’s always takes me out a bit. And then at risk of sounding too harsh, she’s not even the greatest actress, imo, so that adds to this sensation of “taking crazy pills” as to why she keeps getting so lucky. Similar to how I felt about Ansel Elgort in wondering how he kept getting all these great parts when he’s always a weaker point. That meta tangent aside, ‘Jimmy Ink’ just takes away from Spike’s development too much by taking this guardian/maternal/big-sisterly role over him. A role that doesn’t feel congruent with everything we got with the last movie. And even if Jimmy Ink was always meant to join in with Spike as the main protagonists—then I think the whole movie needs to angle more into some theme with her character. Give a reason why Spike is a wallflower(while not undoing development) and make Jimmy Ink more of the focus of this movie, give a theme to Jimmy Ink’s story and the movie as a whole. That’s something I think Danny Boyle excels at—using a story to tell a different story. I believe that’s a big part of what makes ‘28 Days Later’(2002) so beloved in the first place and why the last entry hit so hard with me. I think that alt story would be found in Jimmy and/or ‘Jimmy Ink’ and it’s just not there. So while Jimmy still gets to play the villain, that leaves ‘Jimmy Ink’/Kellyman as this weird tacked on protagonist that feels oddly reminiscent of all her other roles. That’s all what wasn’t working for me, so what was working for me was Ralph Fiennes’ goddamn doctor—Ian Kelson. I love this character so much. Last year was such a good year for amazing characters with Dr. Kelson & ‘One Battle After Another’s Sensei. The poster for this movie filled me with such anxiety over the fate of Dr. Kelson—which though that ends up true, I very much loved the bang he goes out on.  I wasn’t really sure where the story Dr. Kelson & Samson was going. I think I, like most people, felt Dr. Kelson was too sympathetic, or rather he acted with too much pacifism towards the infected. That his choice to not kill them like everyone else does was bound to bite him back in the end. So Samson—this hulking mammoth of a man—returning to him felt like spillover from last movie where our protagonists sparked his rage by keeping the baby and now he came again cause Kelson stopping him made him angrier. But man, I just love the development of Samson actually liking the calmness of Dr. Kelson’s darts and that leading to a therapeutic friendship of Samson getting sedated and listening to the smoothing talks of a great man like Dr. Kelson. Really it’s Dr. Kelson’s interactions with everyone that I love. His with Spike, the mom, Samson and it’s his talk with Jimmy which was, for me, that “best moment” for Jimmy’s character. That Jimmy kinda comes upfront about his situation and that just turns into a therapy session with Dr. Kelson as he unravels everything to him. He even wants to leave Dr. Kelson in peace cause he likes him so much, just giving him a small favor to reaffirm his cult leadership. And if that moment wasn’t good enough, that leads into the greatest moment of this movie—Dr. Kelson putting a human video performance spectacular with special effects and faith shaking imagery. I brought up how it was telegraphed earlier with Dr. Kelson dancing to some music after a day’s work, but my friend made the apt remark that the performance seemed too amazing that dude had to have hoped to perform something spectacular in his Bone Temple. I love this sequence so much, it makes the whole movie worthwhile. Much as I picked apart the shortcomings and thought of this movie as a “stripped down” version of the oddity that is the last movie—this is where all that weirdness went. Dr. Kelson posing as Satan as he lip syncs to Iron Maiden is a glorious sight. It’s fun to see how he rattles all the remaining Jimmies. How Jimmy knows this is all an act but he’s immensely impressed that Dr. Kelson pulled out all the stops and went far above whatever he imagined the mild mannered Dr. Kelson capable of. Then it comes to and though I’m sad Dr. Kelson dies, I think he goes out on a wonderful note in saving Spike from Jimmy’s grasp—blowing up Jimmy’s whole “cult” and virtually saving everyone. It’s really just some A+ usage of that amazing character. What also shocked me and kinda enthralled me for the next movie—moreso than Cillian Murphy’s return, was Samson evolving into something new. I think it’s a feat of the storytelling that Dr. Kelson’s efforts to reach through this virus actually surprise me as Samson breaks through and finds his humanity. That everything we learn about the Rage Virus is actually interesting, not just some throwaway “zombie science”. That it makes some sense as to why Samson returned to Dr. Kelson every day. That the tranq dart took away some of the horrifying imagery the infected seemingly see and scares them into anger. Samson finally becoming whole was just so awesome. A jacked mountain of a zombie man that’s now mild mannered and capable of using all that he passively learned through his life as a rage monster—that’s gonna be so dope to see followed up. Hell even more than the last(partially cause the last ends with the fucking weird ‘Power Rangers’ shit) I’m kinda pumped to see where this story goes. How a superhuman like Samson will take what he may’ve learned from Kelson and possibly lead to a cure or rather the birth of a new kinda race of functional zombie people. Perhaps this movie does follow its predecessor’s footsteps in being a mixed back. Having some evident lows by my standards and tremendous highs. What I didn’t like, I didn’t hate, but I really don’t care for—and that unfortunately is the bulk of the movie. But what I did like, I very much loved watching and loved seeing where it took us. Ultimately, it is a solid sequel to a revival-sequel. It accomplishes what it needed to most in progressing the overall story and inciting interest in a sequel. So much so that the sight Cillian Murphy and his daughter that’s assumedly with Naomie Harris(hope she comes back too), that was just kinda the cherry on top, not the sole reason for want a sequel.

title: Anaconda
my_review: I feel like the trailers did a number of disservices to this movie. I had my own expectations, but this wasn’t quite as bad as I was bracing for from the reception I was seeing it getting. For me, I thought this movie was full meta. I thought Jack Black & Paul Rudd were going to be playing themselves and this was some weird meta reboot about the fact that they’re making a reboot. It did turn out to basically be just that, but without the megastar fourth wall break and there’s instead a fairly wholesome story of friends living out a childhood dream. I think the trailer teed this up to be that full meta/raunch and it’s just not really that great at being that and that’s kinda what lets you down while watching it. This movie kinda has this weird balancing act with how meta leaning they get and just plainly making a pretty mediocre anaconda movie. For most of it, it’s kinda just a pleasant and earnest movie of friends reconnecting and having fun. It’s best for me when it’s just them trying to make the movie, with maybe weird callbacks like having a Jon Voight like character on the boat with them. But then it goes buck wild with it and lends itself far more to a raunchier comedy—akin to something like ‘The Interview’(2014), or ‘This Is The End’(2013), but like a raunch level that would be safe to air on FX without censoring anything. I think there was alot of potential here. In someways it feels like a complete, but now hacked story fit into a “popular” IP like ‘Anaconda’. The friends making a movie is the only thing that gets delivered on while everything else is untapped potential. Daniela Melchior feels nonexistent in this movie—maybe for the better as she’s not that great when she does exist, but when she makes her heel turn it’s just dumb and probably unintentionally meta as being so dumb. The snake handler is a fun character that dies far too soon as he should have made it to the end to kill or keep him, have some weird thing with the giant anaconda. Hell they have an entire film crew out there making the exact same movie they are and they’re all dead the next time we see them. Ice Cube himself makes the expected cameo and it’s fun, except he promptly leaves the movie—like what the fuck—aren’t they all trying to beat the giant anaconda? They then save a J-Lo cameo for the stinger to maybe tease a sequel? I dunno, but it’s INCREDIBLY obvious that both, she wasn’t really available for this movie and if anything, her and Cube felt like last minute additions. There’s just a wealth of missed opportunities with this. That said, I don’t hate this movie. This would be a solid redbox rental choice for the night. Like it was very dumb, but I did get a laugh out of needing to pee on Jack Black. It could have leaned harder any which way and really had something, but as it is, it’s just an alright watch for the night with a trailer that might lead you into thinking some way otherwise.
